reasoning_summary: The configuration matches the question. Re = 0.15*0.01/1.5e-5 = 100. The force reference values (magUInf 0.15, lRef 0.01, Aref 0.0001, rhoInf 1.2) are consistent with the specification. The inlet was measured as uniform (ux_nonuniformity 0.0, uy_max_abs 0.0).

The domain is large and the flow is unbounded in effect. It extends 30D upstream, 50D downstream and 40D half-height, with a blockage ratio of 0.0125. The outlet and lateral boundary conditions are standard, and mass imbalance is negligible (8.3333e-11).

The numerics are adequate. The time scheme is second-order (backward) and convection is linearUpwind. Max Courant is 0.73373 with dt = 0.01 convective units, giving 611.87 steps per shedding period. checkMesh passed (max non-orthogonality 43.313 deg, max skewness 0.53384). The mesh has 160 cells around the cylinder and a wall first cell of 0.005D.

The statistics are well converged. The transient ended at 70.794 convective units and the averaging window starts at 75, so the window is stationary. It holds 12 cycles. The 95% CI on mean Cd is 2.3394e-05, drift is 8.2286e-05 and the half-window difference is 3.847e-05, all far below the 3% tolerance.

The two quantities are consistent across methods and windows. Mean Cd is 1.3313 as reported and 1.3311 in the stationary window. St is 0.16344 (reported), 0.16343 (time-domain) and 0.16344 (FFT). rms Cl is 0.22858 and the Cl amplitude is 0.32338. These agree with a sinusoidal signal, since 0.32338/sqrt(2) is about 0.2287.

Residual risk: this is a single run with no mesh or domain refinement comparison. The wake is coarse far downstream (last cell 1.0209D), and the 1.25% blockage is not quantified. Discretization error against the 3% tolerance therefore can't be bounded directly. Everything else is well controlled, so I accept with medium confidence.
